methodology.title: Stage 3: On-Policy Distillation with Per-Prompt Teacher Dispatch
methodology.detail: Each student rollout prompt is routed to the corresponding frozen domain teacher, which provides token-level log-probabilities. The student is optimized via a reverse KL loss between its policy and the dispatched teacher’s policy.

methodology.title: Loss Implementations
methodology.detail: Two loss variants are used: (1) a policy-gradient form with clipped per-token advantages derived from log-probability differences, compatible with PPO/GRPO frameworks; (2) a top-k distillation loss that uses the teacher’s top-k tokens to reduce variance and infrastructure load.

methodology.title: Infrastructure Optimization
methodology.detail: Teacher prefill computations are decoupled from the RL training loop to reduce latency and complexity, enabling efficient per-token log-probability retrieval during distillation.

mechanism.title: On-Policy Distillation via Reverse KL Loss
mechanism.detail: The student policy π_θ is optimized to minimize the reverse KL divergence to the dispatched teacher policy π_φd on the student’s own rollout distribution, expressed as L_rev-KL = E_{x,y~π_θ}[∑_t π_φd(y_t) log(π_θ(y_t))], ensuring dense token-level supervision and stable policy updates.

mechanism.title: Advantage Clipping for Stability
mechanism.detail: The per-token advantage Â_MOPD,t = clip(log π_φd(y_t) - log π_θ(y_t), -A_max, +A_max) is clipped on both sides to prevent large gradient variance and stabilize training within policy-gradient frameworks.

mechanism.title: Top-k Token Distillation Correction
mechanism.detail: The top-k distillation loss includes an additional term π_φd(v) - π_θ(v) beyond the standard reverse KL to correct bias from truncating the teacher’s distribution to top-k tokens, ensuring the loss is minimized when the student matches the teacher on these tokens.

experiments.title: Capability Integration on Qwen3-30B-A3B
experiments.detail: Evaluated on three domains: Math (AIME25, AIME26), Instruction Following (IFBench, IFEval), and Software Engineering (SWE-bench Verified). Baselines include Mix-RL, Cascade RL, Off-Policy Finetune, and Param-Merge. Metrics are per-domain accuracy and a normalized score that scales performance relative to the Stage-1 student and Stage-2 specialist teachers.

experiments.title: Baseline Comparisons
experiments.detail: MOPD outperforms all baselines by 5.5 normalized score points, closing 91–95% of the gap between the Stage-1 student and specialized RL teachers, demonstrating superior multi-domain capability integration.

experiments.title: Loss Variant Ablations
experiments.detail: Both policy-gradient and top-k loss implementations perform comparably, validating the flexibility of MOPD’s distillation approach.

experiments.title: Industrial Deployment
experiments.detail: MOPD was deployed in the post-training of MiMo-V2-Flash, an industrial-scale frontier LLM, where it matched or exceeded teacher performance on most benchmarks, demonstrating practical scalability.

findings.title: Superior Integration Performance
findings.detail: MOPD leads all baselines on Qwen3-30B-A3B with a normalized score improvement of 5.5 points, effectively inheriting nearly all capabilities of each domain teacher.

findings.title: Exposure Bias Elimination
findings.detail: Training on the student’s own rollouts removes exposure bias inherent in off-policy finetuning, contributing to stable and effective capability integration.

findings.title: Stable and Parallelizable Training
findings.detail: Policy-space integration via per-prompt routing avoids unstable weight-space fusion and enables parallel, independent teacher development.

findings.title: Loss Implementation Flexibility
findings.detail: Both policy-gradient and top-k distillation loss forms yield comparable results, offering trade-offs between variance and infrastructure complexity.

findings.title: Multi-Round Student-Teacher Evolution
findings.detail: The pipeline supports iterative improvement cycles between student and teachers, enhancing capability integration over multiple rounds.

contributions: Proposed MOPD, a novel multi-teacher on-policy distillation paradigm for LLM capability integration.
Demonstrated elimination of exposure bias by training on student rollouts with per-prompt teacher dispatch.
Developed two efficient loss implementations (policy-gradient and top-k) for stable distillation.
Empirically validated MOPD’s superiority over four strong baselines on a large-scale LLM across three diverse domains.
Showcased practical deployment of MOPD in industrial-scale LLM post-training with MiMo-V2-Flash.
limitations: Lack of detailed analysis on the impact of teacher quality variance on student performance.
No reported experiments scaling MOPD beyond three domains to assess scalability limits.
Limited discussion on computational cost and latency trade-offs in large-scale deployments.
Absence of theoretical guarantees or formal convergence analysis for the distillation process.
open_questions: How does MOPD scale with an increasing number of domain teachers and more heterogeneous capabilities?
What are the effects of teacher model quality and domain overlap on the final student performance?
Can MOPD be extended to incorporate dynamic teacher updates or online teacher-student co-training?
How does the choice between policy-gradient and top-k loss variants affect convergence speed and final model robustness?
